title: Prove the exact finite-width slice-call/addition tradeoff (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

For one dense m-axis complex transform at width f, the exact binary-addition minimum with at most s<=m tied slice calls is

```text
A_min(m,f,s) = f*(m-s)
first impossible width for fixed A and s<m = floor(A/(m-s))+1
```

Claim type: scoped written mathematical proof with exact finite corroboration. The support lower bound permits arbitrary monomial free maps and unlimited zero helpers. The attaining construction uses one zero helper, free copies/resets and explicitly width-aware individual-column permutations. It does not supply an attaining word in the narrower tied-column engine.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Jacob Alan Sussman #4628 at `ee4fd87f064017c23e5a86fc1dcfe0a5237caed3` supplies the asymptotic support argument and width-one scratch example. The new step is the sharp addition/call resource law and its explicit finite-width consequence. Credit eumemic #288, Swapnil Jain, Jose Manuel #2108 and the retained register-model lineage. The elementary support-counting technique itself is not claimed as new.

## Evidence

- Before: #4628 section 4 gives an eventual support-growth contradiction for an all-width program with too few calls and a fixed mixing structure.
- After: an exact lower bound and matching width-aware construction, including the full copy/shift/add/reset invoice. The pilot m=3,f=2,s=2 needs exactly two additions.
- All 33 construction operators pass on all 1,928 input columns, with the helper returned to zero. Independent Hamming-distance coefficients give the expected targets. Separate subset expansion checks 26 paid-tensor cases and 770 input columns. Eight invalid-input controls and seven operation mutations reject.
- Local registered replay passes in 1.48 seconds. Each warning-strict direct normal/optimized command takes about 0.61 seconds. CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, standard library only. These are timeout measurements, not a performance claim.
- `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` with full source-history checking passes for all five files at `5fcfa050f2fc5445d7f0997206c5044b17f7e88f`. Official committed export and integrity check pass. Git-free normal/optimized exported replays produce byte-identical generated receipts. Whitespace and Python syntax/function-size inspection pass.

From the repository root, using the exact local interpreter path:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/finite-width-call-mixing-tradeoff
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/finite-width-call-mixing-tradeoff/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/finite-width-call-mixing-tradeoff/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/finite-width-call-mixing-tradeoff --check-source-history
```

The scientific marker is `PASS_FINITE_WIDTH_CALL_MIXING_TRADEOFF no_new_kappa`. `--emit-receipt` prints generated JSON bound to all five source-file hashes; no receipt is handwritten and normal replay writes nothing.

## Limitations

The universal result is the written support proof, not an exhaustive enumeration of programs. Finite replay corroborates the stated bounded domain. The upper construction assumes individual-column permutations, zero scratch and free singular resets. It does not cover arbitrary dirty helper restoration, prove a multi-output direct-sum law, settle the small-saving cases of #4628, or give physical tape/precision/compiler/ownership pricing. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Lean, selected cold replay and full multiplication-theorem obligations were not run. There is no new supplier, kappa or selected-frontier change.

## Open next questions

- Determine the tradeoff with tied-column free permutations, starting at m=2,f=2. The individual-column shifts used here are forbidden there.
- Determine the reversible dirty-helper tradeoff for one remaining bit. The copied and reset zero helper does not supply a dirty return word.

## Related open work

- #4628 studies lower bounds for the same complex slice-transform family. This quantifies its one-output support argument and gives a matching construction in an explicitly wider finite-width model; its hook ranks, numerical bounds and small open shapes are not rechecked or settled.
